mode: first real Windows capture attempt (2 files, run by hand with Wireshark/dumpcap, not capture.ps1, connecting/disconnecting on two different physical USB ports) + Axis Studio license check
hypothesis: does either capture contain the hub's handshake, and can Axis Studio connect to the hub at all
verdict: double negative, both diagnosed. (1) Capture: zero PNHU01 frames in either file - only a generic USB hub (VID 0x214b) and a Logitech Unifying receiver (VID 0x046d PID 0xc534) were captured; the hub's real CP210x (VID 0x10c4 PID 0xea60) never appeared. Root cause: picking one USBPcap interface by hand per run is exactly the trap capture.ps1 exists to avoid - the hub was on a controller other than the interface chosen. (2) License: Axis Studio (already installed, current PN3/Studio generation) requires a paid activation the owner doesn't have. Static analysis of its binaries for reusable protocol/CRC-8 structures came up empty - no v1-era markers (PNHU/CP210/Silicon Labs) anywhere, only current-generation model codes (N3T/U1H/U2H/U2P), so Axis Studio most likely dropped support for PNHU01 entirely - not worth analyzing further. Researched the activation system (403 on direct fetch to noitom.com/support.neuronmocap.com, pieced together from search snippets): current activation (account.noitom.com, Product ID) doesn't apply to this hardware generation; legacy activation used a physical Wibu dongle and Noitom appears to have stopped issuing new activations for it entirely.

mode: wrote scripts/crc8-search.py: brute-force every (byte-region x poly x init x refin x refout x xorout) CRC-8 combination, and simple XOR/sum checksums, against the 508 real frames from T009, filtered to the well-typed Call/Ack/Value/Data/Set frames (375, after excluding firmware-blob noise and frames mis-split by an internal 0xfd/0xfe byte collision)
hypothesis: can the CRC-8 algorithm that T004/T006 established was never published anywhere be recovered now that real (message, crc) pairs exist, instead of guessing blind
verdict: CONFIRMED, the CRC-8 mystery is solved: poly=0x07 (the plain/standard CRC-8 polynomial), init=0x00, no bit reflection, computed over [type,id,src,dst,cmd,payload...] (frame[1:-2], i.e. everything between the 0xfd SOF and the CRC byte), then the result is XORed with a constant 0xFD to get the final CRC byte. Matches 368/375 (98%) of the filtered real frames exactly. The 7 exceptions are all short/irregular sub-frames (e.g. Acks with a 5-byte body instead of the usual 9, one 17-byte Data frame, one 18-byte frame that may itself be leftover noise) - not yet explained, but too small and too structurally different to doubt the core algorithm. crc8-search.py kept in scripts/ for rerunning against future captures (e.g. to explain the 7 stragglers, or once a real 'Connect' capture exists).

mode: 3 parallel research agents: (1) mine ../reverb-g2 for reusable ideas, (2) Wine/Proton compatibility for legacy Axis Neuron, (3) live-streaming Axis Neuron's motion data into Unity/a game engine
hypothesis: does the sibling project have transferable methodology we haven't used yet, is Wine a viable way to run Axis Neuron long-term instead of a real Windows box, and is there a documented way to get live mocap data into Unity without waiting on the full protocol reverse-engineering effort
verdict: three distinct answers. (1) reverb-g2: no direct Wine/game-engine/licensing precedent (different problem shape - HP's driver isn't dongle-gated), but its whole thesis validates this project's Path A priority: reverse-engineer once, then run natively, don't keep depending on a vendor Windows app long-term. (2) Wine: zero WinehQ AppDB entries or community reports for Axis Neuron either way; the CP210x/tty passthrough mechanism itself is well-documented and should work in principle, but one real risk surfaced (a Wine bug capping reported serial baud rate at 115200, which could silently break high-rate IMU streaming) - untested, not to be relied on without trying it empirically first. (3) Unity: real, documented, license-free path exists and doesn't require any of the protocol reverse-engineering - legacy Axis Neuron has built-in BVH Broadcasting (Settings > Broadcasting, TCP/UDP ports 7001 raw BVH / 7003 calculated data, with an 'Axis Legacy' skeleton-type option matching this exact PN32/PNHU01 hardware generation), consumable in Unity via the open-source keijiro/NeuronAnimator plugin or Noitom's own official Unity SDK package - both just connect to that broadcast, no Axis Studio and no license needed. A community VRPN fork (vrpn-PerceptionNeuron, explaining the vrpnNoitom.dll seen in docs/04's static analysis) exists but talks to the hub directly via hidapi, bypassing Axis Neuron entirely - same reverse-engineering problem as this project, not a shortcut, not worth pursuing separately.

mode: wrote scripts/pn-send.py: construct a real Call frame (GetConfig, key=HubFirmwareVersion) using the CRC-8 formula from T010, send it to the hub via /dev/ttyUSB0 with pyserial, across the same baud rates T003/T006 already knew about but this time actively sending (T006 only ever sent at 115200)
hypothesis: does the hub actually respond to a frame we constructed ourselves (not replayed from a capture), confirming the CRC-8 algorithm and framing end-to-end, and is 115200 baud - the only rate T006 tried while sending - actually the wrong baud for TX
verdict: CONFIRMED, full round trip working from Linux for the first time. 115200: no response (as T006 found). 921600 (and 1000000/3000000, which the cp210x driver evidently coerces towards the chip's real max rather than rejecting): hub replied `fd0200c0a002010200000079fe` (Ack) then `fd0400c0a0010f00100b021415 91fe` (Data) - byte-for-byte the same Ack/Data shape seen in the real T009 capture, and the firmware-version byte inside correctly reads 0x15 (21) instead of the pre-upgrade capture's 0x14 (20), matching the T008 firmware upgrade exactly. This independently confirms the CRC-8 formula (docs/05) is exactly right, and identifies the missing piece T006 never varied: send baud must be 921600, not 115200 - 115200 only ever worked for the passive listen probe (T003), never for transmit.

mode: sent the two Function-cmd candidate payloads from pneuron.lua's comments (03 0d 00 01 00 'connect?', 02 00 00 00 00 'disconnect?') via scripts/pn-send.py at 921600 baud, hub connected but no sensor straps attached
hypothesis: does either candidate elicit a distinct, meaningful response confirming it as the real connect/disconnect command, now that framing/CRC/baud are all confirmed working (T012)
verdict: both got real Ack+Value responses (no timeouts, no garbage) - the hub is not just ignoring unrecognized Function payloads. 'connect' candidate: Ack echoes the sent payload as expected, but the Value response payload differs from the sent bytes (03 07 01 07 00, not an echo) - the hub computed something. 'disconnect' candidate: both Ack and Value responses are plain echoes of the sent payload (02 00 00 00 00) - no computed content, consistent with 'nothing to disconnect' in this fresh state. Not fully decoded yet - no sensor straps were attached, so even a real successful connect wouldn't necessarily start a visible IMU stream. Next: attach straps and repeat, and/or capture a real Connect from Axis Neuron's main window (not just the Upgrade dialog used for T009) to compare against these candidates byte-for-byte.
